title: One step of Euler integration
instructions:
## The simulation loop, one step at a time

A ball is thrown straight up at **10 m/s** with g = 9.8 m/s² and a time step of **0.5 s**.

1. Explicit Euler: y₁ = y₀ + v₀·dt, then v₁ = v₀ − g·dt. What is y₁?
2. Semi-implicit (symplectic) Euler: update the velocity first, then y₁ = y₀ + v₁·dt. What is y₁?
3. The exact height at t = 0.5 s (y = v₀t − ½gt²).
4. The exact maximum height.
5. The time to the apex.
hints: Explicit Euler uses the old velocity: 10 × 0.5 = 5.
Max height = v₀² / (2g); time to apex = v₀ / g.

realityNote: Explicit Euler gains energy every step (the ball flies higher each bounce); semi-implicit Euler loses a little and stays stable, which is why most game engines use it, with a fixed time step so the physics is the same on every phone.
